findings.title: Detach background writes from request cancellation
findings.body: The legacy write's timeout context is derived from the request context. The HTTP server cancels that parent when the request handler returns, so returning the unified-storage result can immediately cancel the background legacy write rather than give it ten seconds to complete. This affects all four asynchronous write methods and can routinely leave legacy storage unchanged after successful requests. Preserve the request's context values while detaching cancellation before applying the background timeout.

findings.title: Preserve write ordering when mirroring to legacy storage
findings.body: Each successful write launches an independent goroutine with no ordering between operations on the same resource. A client can successfully create an object and then delete it, while the legacy delete executes before the legacy create finishes; the create then leaves an object in legacy storage that is absent from unified storage. Consecutive updates can likewise overwrite newer data with older data. Background mirroring needs ordered execution or another mechanism that prevents stale operations from being applied.

findings.title: Mirror the resolved update rather than replaying UpdatedObjectInfo
findings.body: The legacy update now receives the original UpdatedObjectInfo instead of a wrapper containing the object returned by unified storage. UpdatedObjectInfo can calculate a PATCH or server-side apply result from the old object supplied by the store. Replaying it against legacy storage, which may be stale because mirroring is asynchronous, can produce a different object or fail even though the unified update succeeded. Pass the resolved unified-storage result to the legacy update, as the previous implementation did, rather than independently recomputing the update against legacy state.

findings.title: Do not use resource names as the kind metric label
findings.body: The successful delete duration passes name in the argument position used for options.Kind by the other metric calls. This creates separate metric series for every deleted resource name rather than a bounded set of kinds, causing unbounded Prometheus cardinality and memory growth as resources are deleted. It also makes successful delete metrics inconsistent with failed delete metrics. Pass the resource kind instead.

findings.title: Attribute duration and error metrics to the store actually called
findings.body: The asynchronous DeleteCollection call records its legacy-store duration and failures through recordStorageDuration, so legacy failures are reported as unified-storage failures and unified-storage timings include legacy work. Conversely, the unified Create and Update error paths at lines 45 and 129 call recordLegacyDuration even though legacy storage was never invoked. Correct these store assignments so operators can distinguish primary-storage failures from failed safety copies.

findings.title: Use distinct store mocks and wait for background assertions
findings.body: The tests give legacy and unified storage the same mock.Mock, so expectations for identically named methods cannot distinguish which store was called. For example, the create failure case configures only setupLegacyFn but that expectation also satisfies the unified Create call. The write tests also return without waiting for or asserting the background legacy calls. As a result, they can pass when writes go to the wrong store or legacy mirroring never happens. Use separate mocks and synchronize assertions on completion of the asynchronous writes.
